data.definition: Resampling by area averaging (`Resample.area`): each output pixel is the mean of the input pixels it covers.
A rectangle of the screen, a view or a page that the code calls an area (a `CGRect`), such as the canvas's bounds inside the chrome.
An area the drawn lines enclose: book cells joined across edges with no line, what the painter reads as one shape (pbn's line-art metrics, `CellMap.mergeSmallWithinAreas`).
A line of text Vision found in the photo, as the box the writing stage reads and traces (`WritingAreaStats`, `Writing.find(in:areas:)`).
In the making-of show: a connected run of one paint in the show's palette picture, as against the merged region it ends up in (`FieldSteps`).

The painter's word for a region: one connected area of one paint, painted with one tap; what UI copy, VoiceOver, the painting screen and Refine call it (`paintArea`, `CanvasAreaElement`, `RefineAreaCard`).
A size: the square canvas units, pixels or points a shape, region, box or canvas covers (`Region.area`, `signedArea`, `minArea`, `maxCanvasArea`).

The painter's saved piece in the gallery: one library folder (meta.json, template, progress, photo, thumbnail) with its metadata `Artwork`, and the store, factory, exports and views on it; the UI copy calls it a painting.
The frame of the canvas or of a map: the margin `LineDetection` clears (the canvas edge is not a line), regions that touch it.
Where two neighbouring cells or regions meet: `CellMap.Pair.border`'s class by the strongest line near it, whether a region borders another (`EditMerge`), what Move Edge drags.

The stretches of the drawing that bound cells, kept apart from the lines drawn inside one (`LayeredLines.Plan.boundaryLines`, `LineArtStats.boundaryLength`); the template's drawn edges are made from them.

Where neighbouring labels differ in a label map or raster, as segmentation smooths, measures or draws it (`BoundarySmoothing`, `RegionAdjacency.boundarySteps`, pbn's `boundaryRaster`, eval's boundaries.png).
The delimiter between the parts of the feedback upload's multipart/form-data body (`FeedbackUploader.makeBoundary`).

The line between two regions of a template: its edges, the graph they are traced into, and the boundaries an edit lays, moves or tests a point against (`BoundaryEdge`, `BoundaryGraph`, `Lattice.Containment.boundary`).
A moment where one stage of the making-of's timeline ends and the next begins, as a test probes them (`TimelineTests`).
A coloring-book cell: a piece of paint the drawing's lines (or an undrawn cell edge) enclose, which becomes one template region; what Refine's Cells tools select, merge and reshape.
A square bin of a grid over the canvas or a picture: a pixel, a spatial-hash bucket, a lattice square of noise or of a test pattern; nothing to do with paint.
A slot of a laid-out table or sheet: a cell of the regression table, a tile of an eval or Auto sheet, a glyph's box in the digit atlas.
A small capsule control or badge on screen: the create flow's Suggested-settings chip (`originChip`, `chipBackground`) and Refine's look chips (`RefineColorsPanel.chip`); not a paint.
A region's paint as its index into `Template.palette` (`Region.colorIndex`); the number printed in the region is this + 1.
Comments only, never a name: the numbers drawn for a color, as in the canvas uniforms' selected-color number opacity and a making-of clip docstring's colors (numbers included).
A channel value of a color, as the array handed to `CGColor(colorSpace:components:)` (`TemplateRasterizer`, `FeedbackPackage`).

A connected set found by labelling: the 4- or 8-connected pixels of one class (`ConnectedComponents.label`, `Components`, `Writing.Patch.components`) or a stroke graph's edges that meet (`StrokeGraph.components`).

The contour map: HED's edge map of a photo's outlines, one of line art's two inputs beside the drawing, whose strength decides the outline layer (`LineArtInput.contours`, `EdgeMap.contourWeight`, `drawingAndContours`).
A closed polygon traced around a shape: an eye's contour (`EyeFinder.Eye.contour`) or a mask's (`MaskContours`), which line art draws as an outline.
When or that something was made, in prose only ("immutable after creation", a stroke path's creation date); code uses only the system's `creationDate`.
The hexadecimal digits of a color code: a palette color's `rrggbb` (`PaletteColor.hexDigits`) or a vocabulary line's.
A digit of a printed paint number: how many a number has and how they are measured, laid out and drawn (`LabelSizing.digitCount`, `digitAdvance`, `DigitAtlas`, `GlyphInstance.digit`).
In the app's making-of: each label's paint number, palette index + 1 (`MakingOfShow.digits`), and the text the view resolves for each.
A file type the app declares in Info.plist (`CFBundleDocumentTypes`), as `tools/strings_check.py` and the app's tests read it.

An artwork's template and saved progress loaded for painting, with a notice to show once (`PaintingDocument`, what `Library.loadForPainting` and `regenerate` return); not the artwork itself (no photo, title or metadata).
A PDF as bytes or as opened again: what `PDFExporter.document(for:title:paper:)` writes and the rendering tests read back page by page.

A template's boundary edge: the shared polyline between two regions (or a region and the outside) from junction to junction (`BoundaryEdge`, `Template.edges`, `EdgeRef`), drawn in its line's layer or, as a color edge, left undrawn.

An undrawn edge between two cells, a color edge where only the paint changes, shown dashed in Refine, and Refine's tools named for edges: Cell Edge lays one, Move Edge drags any border (`TemplateEditor.Edit.cellEdge`, `RefineCellEdges`).

The edge map: an 8-bit picture of a photo's lines (HED's contours, the line-drawing network's drawing, combined) that line art is traced from, and its detector (`EdgeMap`, `EdgeDetector`, `LineArtInput.edges`, `usesEdgeMap`).

An edge of a graph: a link between nodes of the line-art pipeline's `StrokeGraph`, or between neighbouring regions or pixels in a segmentation merge or spanning tree (`BandMerging`, `TextureConsolidation`).

An edge in a picture rather than in the template: where a photo's color or a mask changes, a paint's or bloom's rim, a raster's or patch's border (`softEdge`, `edgeSigma`, `DomainTransformFilter`'s `edgeScale`, `Writing.reachesEdge`).
A side of the screen, a view or a popover in SwiftUI layout, and the margin kept from it (`Toast.edge`, `GentleTipModifier.arrowEdge`, a swipe from the screen's edge).
One item of a collection: a cache's or string catalog's entry, a color key line, a baseline record, a directory listing item, an edit file's paint.
Where a picture comes in from in the Start hand-off and the making-of show: the rect its motion starts at (`StartHandoffPlan.entry`, `MakingOfView.entry`, `captureEntry`).

The dark the drawing's lines and the numbers are drawn in, on the canvas, in pictures and print and in Refine, and where it lies (`CanvasUniforms.ink`, `TemplateEditor.inkWidth`, `PaletteBar.numeralInk`, `inkDistance`).
The painter's PencilKit marks on a feedback screenshot: their ink, colors and what lies under them (`FeedbackInk`, `FeedbackInkColor`, `FeedbackPackage.Ink`, `FeedbackDraft.hasInk`).

In the making-of show and its Python reference: the drawing inked over the picture, its step, timing, ramp, grey and coverage (`InkLine`, `InkCoverage`, `ScheduleTiming.inkStep`, `ShowSpec.Outlines.inkRamp`).
The dark strokes of letters in the photo, which the writing stage finds, measures and paints out before segmenting (`Writing.Ink`, `Writing.nearInk`, `minimumInk`, `WritingAreaStats.inkPerLength`).
The canvas's VoiceOver elements and rotor results (`CanvasView.accessibleItems`).
One credited acknowledgement (`Acknowledgement`) as its row shows it or `AboutTests` checks it.

One element of a list, map, heap, bucket or directory listing being iterated, popped or chosen (a loop's `item`, Python's `.items()`, `MinHeap.Item`, `PaletteOrdering.Item`), and SwiftUI's `item:` presentation labels in Refine.
A test's `ArtworkDraft`: a new artwork's contents built and handed to `Library.create`.
A photo the system picker hands the create flow (`PhotosPickerItem`): the one picked, browsed or in the embedded picker's selection.
The optional value whose presence shows a sheet (SwiftUI's `.sheet(item:)`), such as a time-lapse request or the artwork being sent.
A bundled library picture the library makes an artwork from at first launch or in a demo, with its painted fraction and age (`Library.SeedItem`, `ShellDemo.galleryItems`).
What a share sheet, ShareLink or file transfer hands on: a file URL, image or exported file (`ActivityShareSheet.items`, `presentedItems`, `GalleryView.shareItems`).
An on-screen button or menu entry a UI test finds and taps (`RefineUITests.menuItem`, a gallery card menu's action).

Where a region's number is drawn: a `Template.Label` (position, free radius, region), the first at the region's pole, and the room, size, placement, moves and checks of it (`LabelSizing`, `LabelRoom`, `moveLabel`).

A region id in a label map: the per-pixel index a segmentation, a connected-components pass or the making-of's labeling gives each connected area (`Segmentation.labels`, `labelMap`, `RegionLabels`, `label_regions`).

A name text attached to a control, view, element or debug object: SwiftUI's `Label` and `label:` builders, VoiceOver's `accessibilityLabel` and `PaintSpeech`'s spoken labels, a Metal pass's or queue's label.
The printed template's color key (`PDFExporter.legend`): for each paint its number, a dot of its color, its nickname or plain name, hex and area count.

One line of a coloring book's drawing: traced from the edge map or writing (`DrawnLine`), in a strength layer (`LineLayer`), stored as drawn edges and interior strokes, inked, and drawn or erased by the painter (`LineEdit`, `drawingLines`).
A straight line the curve fitter fits through a run of lattice points (`CurveFitter.fitLines`, `lineNormal`, `lineOffset`), and digital straight lines.

Line art: a template's drawing as a whole and what makes, stores and reports it: its settings, inputs and maps, the `LINE` chunk, its checks and stats (`TemplateLineArt`, `LineArtSettings`, `LineArtInput`, `LineArtStats`).

How a line or path is stroked: its width, weight, opacity, color and mode, for the drawing's ink (Settings › Line Weight, `CanvasUniforms.lineWidth`) and for any drawn path (`ProgressRing.lineWidth`).
The create flow's Lines slider: how much of the drawing a template keeps, from only the strongest edges to the faintest (`CreateModel.lines`, saved as `CreateDraft.lines`).
A row of swatches in the painting screen's palette bar: how many rows it lays out and fits (`PaletteBar`'s lines, `PaletteRows.maxLines`, `paletteLines`).
A line of text Vision found in the photo, which the writing stage traces, paints out and keeps numbers off (`TextFinder.lines(in:)`, `TemplateRefinements.textLine`, `Writing.joinLines`).
One row of a raster that a separable pass works through at a time (`DistanceTransform`, `Resample`, `StructureMap`).
A line of text a program reads, writes or sets: of a source or data file, log, report, table, caption or PDF color key (`FeedbackReport`'s lines, `strings_check.py`, `PDFExporter.line`).

A paint's playful name ("Harbor Fog"), derived at load from its OKLab, the artwork's seed and a frozen vocabulary version, never stored (`ColorNickname`, `nicknameVersion`, `nicknameSeed`, `colorNicknames`).

A paint number as printed in its region: its glyphs on the canvas, in pictures, the SVG and the making-of, where it sits, its size, ink, timing and whether it shows (`showsNumbers`, `numberColor`, `ShowTemplate.Number`, `moveNumber`).

A number in the everyday sense, not a paint's: a value read from a flag, spec, mailbox or JSON (`pbn`'s `number(_:_:)`, `ShowSpec.number`), an ordinal of a feedback mark, test move or area, JavaScript's `Number`.

A paint's number, its palette index + 1, by which regions, swatches, VoiceOver, the palette's order, Refine's cards and feedback reports name a paint (`PaintSpeech.colorLabel(number:)`, `FeedbackReport.Paint.number`, `selectedNumber`).
A paint number as set in New York on a swatch or the canvas: its ink, font and size (`PaletteBar.numeralInk`, `PaletteMetrics.numeralSize`, `DigitAtlas.numeralFont`).

The lines a renderer draws between regions: every boundary edge and, for line art, the interior strokes, with their color, width, opacity and pass (`OutlineGeometry`, `CanvasSnapshot.Options.outlines`, `outlineWidth`, `Theme.outline`).

The drawing's strongest layer (`LineLayer.outline`): strong edges, eyes and subjects' silhouettes, set by `outlineThreshold`, `outlineEyes`, `outlineObjects`; by default the only lines that split same-paint cells.

A region's or shape's boundary as a closed curve: the rings an edit redraws and checks numbers against, a polygon a label or a shape keeps to (`EditWork.locate.onOutline`, `Template.outlineDistance`, `LocalOutline`, `crownOutline`).
The making-of show's outline step: the drawing inked over the picture, with its spec, schedule and ink lines (`ShowSpec.Outlines`, `Outlines.swift`, `OutlinesTests`).
A paint's number, palette index + 1, spelled out: what comments call it and what `RefineUITests.paintNumber(in:)` reads from an area card's label.

The photo's color of a piece a drawn line cuts, read before the line is laid and kept in the edit (`TemplateEditor.Paint`: a point and an OKLab color; `painted`, an edit's `paints`, pbn's `EntryPaint`).

One entry of a template's palette, the color the painter paints with, numbered palette index + 1: what code, UI copy and VoiceOver call a paint (`paints`, `samePaint`, `paintsMerged`, `currentPaint`).
A feedback report's row for one paint as the painter saw it: its number, hex, structured name and nickname (`FeedbackReport.Paint`, `FeedbackReport.Painting.paints`).
In the making-of show and its Python reference: one color of the show's palette picture, with its seeds, flow and timing (`PaintSeed`, `PaintColors`, `PaintFlow`, `paint_of`).

Painting as an act: filling areas with their paint, on the painting screen and in its types, events, progress and animation (`PaintingSession.paint`, `PaintView`, `PaintProgress`, `PaintTips`, `paintArea`).

The template drawn as painted, every area (or every one painted so far) in its paint: a rendering style and the image or rect it gives (`TemplateRasterizer.Style.painting`, `PreviewStyle.painting`, `paintingPNG`).

Painting as an activity: filling areas on the painting screen and what drives, times, sounds or paces it (`PaintingSession`, `PaintingFocus`, `PaintingMelody`, `PaintingTime`, `PaintingLength`); not the piece.

The UI copy's word for an artwork, the painter's saved piece: what the gallery opens, deletes, sends and receives (`SharedPainting`), loads (`PaintingDocument`) and counts as free or unlimited (`FreePaintings`).
One entry of `Template.palette`: a paint's OKLab and encoded RGB (`PaletteColor`, with its structured name and hex); what comments and VoiceOver's catalog comments call a palette color.
One element of a template's palette as pbn's comments name it: for a flat-color input, each distinct color.
A paint's index into `Template.palette`, as comments and the shader's `w` name `Region.colorIndex`; no identifier is spelled so.
The canvas chrome's colors for one paper and system appearance: background, paper, ink, shadow, rim and accent limits (`CanvasPalette`, `canvasPalette`), not the template's paints.

The palette as the painter sees it: the painting screen's and Refine's bar of swatches, its rows, order, layout and metrics, and an eval sheet's palette strip (`PaletteBar`, `PaletteOrder`, `RefinePalette`).
The palette picture: the working image flattened to the template's paints, the snapshot the making-of show and its Python reference read (`ShowPictures.palette`, `paletteGrey`, `paletteLabels`).

The ordered paints a photo is reduced to: a template's or segmentation's `[PaletteColor]`, a paint's number its index + 1, as built, ordered and measured (`Template.palette`, `paletteCount`, `PaletteBuilder`).
A flat swatch of one color in a picture: a test image's colored patch, a patch of photo or canvas a test averages.
The writing stage's window around one line of text, read on a finer raster than the canvas so small letters keep their shapes (`Writing.Patch`).
A picture of the picture library (a `Sample`: a public-domain painting or photograph shipped with the app), its credits row, listing and placeholder (`isPicture`, `ShellDemo.pictures`, `PictureRow`).
In the making-of show: a stage image of the pipeline the show is built from and composites, and its recipe (`ShowPictures`, `PipelineSnapshot.Picture`, `PictureRecipe`, the Python's `*_picture`).

An image the app renders or shows and the rect it fills: the create flow's preview layer (`CreateModel.Picture`) and its travel into the painting, Refine's canvas picture, feedback's pictures, test renders.
One area a drawn line or edge cuts a region into, before it becomes a region of its own (`EditWork.Piece`); a drawn line's paints are the photo's colors of these.
A connected bit of traced writing: a stroke between ends and junctions, or a dot (`WritingAreaStats.piecesPerHeight`, `Writing.maximumPieces`).
A stretch of a line, path or curve between cuts: what `pieces(keeping:)` keeps, an eraser leaves, a reshape moves or a curve is cut into.

A run of points joined by straight segments, as plain geometry: an edge's smoothed points (`EdgePolylines`), a run added to a path (`addPolyline`, `RefineInkLayer.polyline`), the making-of's `Polyline`.
Part of a design-system token's name (`pot-3-gold`), cited in `Theme`; not a paint.
A word of a nickname in the vocabulary table ("Terracotta Pot"); not a code concept.
Projecting a point onto a guide line: the nearest point's distance and parameter along it (`EdgeGuides.Guide.project`).
The app's Xcode project (`App/PaintByNumber.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj`) and its build settings, as `tools/strings_check.py` reads and tests them.
The device's locale region (`Locale.Region`), which picks the paper a printed template is laid out for (`PDFExporter.Paper.default(for:)`).
In the making-of show and its Python reference: a connected run of one color in one of the show's pictures (`Labeling.regions`, `RegionLabels`), simplified or merged, timed by `regionTimes`.
One connected area of one paint: a label of the segmentation's region map and, in the template, an entry of `Template.regions` (rings, number, fill), the unit the painter paints and progress counts.
A value held aside in memory to restore or compare with later: `EditBrush`'s state before a trial, a test's generated template before encoding.
A time-lapse replayed from an artwork in the store (`TimelapseSource.saved(store:artwork:)`), as against an open painting's live state.
What is on disk, as last written or read back, or whether a write landed: an artwork's progress (`ArtworkStore.SavedProgress`), a draft, meta or file bytes, the revision the autosaver last wrote.
A straight piece of a line or polyline between two consecutive points: an outline's GPU segment, a curve's span, the piece of an edge or stroke a pen, eraser or check touches.

The segmentation stage, photo to region label map and palette: `Segmenter.segment`, its test helper `TestScenes.segment`, its `StageClock` names (`segment.*`) and where its progress ends (`segmentEnd`).
A segment in a platform's sense, not geometry: a segmented control's button in a UI test, a URL path's segment in the feedback relay.
An array's dimensions: a NumPy array's or a Core ML tensor's `shape` (height, width, channels).
How a boundary edge's points were made, in the smoother's order of preference: drawn, faired, fitted, midpoints or lattice (`EdgeSmoother.Shape`).
The closed outline of a region or of an area lines close, as rings, polygons or a path (`RegionShapes`, `CreateModel.ClosedShape`, a mask's traced contours).
A figure Refine's Shapes tool draws as a line: a straight line, rectangle, oval, curve, hexagon or star (`RefineShape`, `ShapePath`).
In the retired crew show's Python planner: how far apart guardians' spots stay while both are there (`SPACE`).
Room on screen: the size a layout is offered, or a named coordinate space (`CompareView.fillsSpace`).
A color space: how encoded RGB maps to color (`RGBColorSpace`, sRGB or Display P3; Core Graphics' `CGColorSpace`).
One test's local name for the template's regions of one paint (`VectorizerTests`): the spots of a dotted test picture.
In the making-of show and its Python planner: a pixel drawn by weight and kept apart from the others, where a seed lands or a guardian worked (`Spot`, `Sampling`).
A mark the painter draws with PencilKit on a feedback screenshot, kept, described and sent with the report (`FeedbackStroke`, `FeedbackMarks`, `FeedbackReport.Stroke`).

A line of the drawing stored inside one region rather than on its boundary (`InteriorStroke`, `TemplateLineArt.strokes`, `strokePoints`, `writingStrokes`): a crease, a strand of fur, an eye inside a cell, traced writing.

One drag of the painter's finger or pencil that paints areas on the painting screen, as the session, progress, tips, timelapse and regeneration's carried-over painting order count it (`PaintingSession.beginStroke`, `strokeEnded`).
Drawing a path's line rather than filling it, through SwiftUI, Core Graphics or a raster helper: a view's `.stroke`, a canvas's `stroke(_:with:style:)`, pbn's `stroke(_:_:width:)`.
A drag on Refine's screen and what it leaves in the painter's refinements: the pen's line, a Paint Brush or eraser pass (`TemplateRefinements.Stroke`, `maximumStrokes`, `RefineView.endStroke`).
In the making-of show and its Python reference: a line of the drawing as the show inks it, with its schedule, timing and stream (`StrokeSchedule`, `ScheduleStyle.strokeEarliest`, `STROKE_SPEED`).
A traced polyline of the line-art pipeline before the template stores it: a thinned ridge's path in `StrokeGraph`, a letter's stroke in `Writing`, measured by `minimumStrokeLength`.
Refine's dot of a pending fill: where the fill was tapped and the photo's color there, shown until the template that has the fill comes (`RefineFillLayer.Swatch`, `showsSwatch`).
A color-naming test fixture's row: a corpus sample's palette color as hex and the structured name it should get (`ColorFixtures.Swatch`, `ColorFixtures.swatches`).

A paint's chip in a palette, its number on its color: the painting screen's and Refine's palette bars (`swatch-N`, `PaletteBar.Swatch`, `SwatchDetails`) and an eval or regression sheet's palette strip.

data.why: One concept, two names: the model and the pipeline say region (`Template.regions`, `PaintingSession`'s `region` indices); the UI copy, VoiceOver, the painting screen and Refine say area (`canvas-area-<region>`, `paintArea`).

One concept under two names: the code calls the saved piece an artwork (`Artwork`, `ArtworkStore`, `artworkID`), while the UI copy, tests and a few types call it a painting ("Delete this painting?", `SharedPainting`, `PaintingDocument`, `FeedbackReport.Painting`).
A border between two cells is a boundary edge (or a run of them) of the template; Refine's copy says border where the code says edge.
The pipeline's boundary lines are the drawing's lines (`DrawnLine`) that bound a cell, before `annotate` gives their layer to the template's edges.
One concept, two names: a template's boundary between two regions is stored as `BoundaryEdge`s (`Template.edges`) and traced in `BoundaryGraph`.
In a coloring book each cell the lines enclose becomes one template region (`LineArtStats.cells == template.regions.count`); Refine's Cells tools and the canvas's hatch comments call regions cells.
`Region.colorIndex` is what comments and the shader call the palette index
The contour map is an `EdgeMap` (HED's), combined with the drawing into `LineArtInput.edges`.
A mask's or eye's traced contour is the closed outline of a shape, as polygons.
`MakingOfShow.digits` holds each label's paint number (palette index + 1) under the name digits
Both name one element of a generic collection (a loop's item, a cache's or listing's entry); neither is a domain concept.
one concept, two names: where a region's number is drawn is a `Label` in PaintCore, a `Number` in the making-of (`ShowTemplate.Number`, one per label) and Refine's Move Number (`.moveLabel`)
Both name a line of text Vision found in the photo, which the writing stage reads and traces.
a numeral is a paint number as drawn in New York, on a swatch or the canvas
Both name the closed boundary of a region or of an area the lines close, as rings, polygons or a path.
the same value spelled out: a paint's number, palette index + 1
`Template.palette` is `[PaletteColor]` and a paint is one of its entries: the stored type and the code's and painter's word for one concept.
pbn's comments call one element of `Template.palette` (a `PaletteColor`) a palette entry.
A test's local name for a set of template regions.
